title: GPOM Second Half C: The Walk Out
heading: GitPush Origin Master ▲ second half C: the walk out
about: After the vote (Kai writes it; all hundred agreed). Maddie leads the hundred out of the bunker and across the downs to the AI's building. Stage 1 written brief: brief.md; music: music.md.
stage: 1 (written brief, no interview: the 2026-10-21 autonomous run, second-half-ending-goal.md)

maddie.rule: ALWAYS this reference; the torn bunting stays in every shot
maddie.voice: Gemini TTS Aoede (Bristol, the plan's bot profile)

ai.rule: No body, ever. Speaks through Maddie's speaker (beacon pulses on his words); the last line of the film is the one unfiltered read
ai.voice: Suno Voice "badcode newsreader" (the AI), dry, through Maddie's speaker: small-speaker filter, beacon pulses on his words

building.rule: ONE fixed design: a long, low building of black glass, many times longer than it is tall, with one single thin horizontal seam of warm amber light running its whole length, set down in a fold between two green chalk downs, the only made thing in sight; no windows, no signs, no other lights
building.note: Design anchor = the BL series (BL1-day, BL2-dusk, BL4-seam-opens, BL5-aerial; second-half-moodboard.md). L11-exterior-night is NOT this design (a tall near-cubic block, seam part-way) and is not used.

beats.name: Off the step
beats.blurb: The blast doors stand open on daylight. The old lady comes out first, stops beside Maddie on the step, straightens her torn bunting, and sends her ahead. Trust given by an act, not a line.

lines.speaker: lady
lines.how: dry, flat, not looking at her; said while her hand is still on the bunting, as if it were nothing

lines.speaker: maddie
lines.voice: Gemini TTS Aoede (Bristol, the plan's bot profile)
lines.how: genuinely touched, trying not to make a fuss

beats.name: Into daylight
beats.blurb: The hundred file out of the hill, blinking. The kill bots' track marks are still gouged in the grass.

beats.name: The long walk
beats.blurb: One unbroken travelling shot: the camera backs along the chalk track and Maddie rolls after it, as on the high street in beat 0, but now a hundred people walk behind her.

beats.name: The seat
beats.blurb: Sandra and Derek, walking. The row, one last time, and what it now means.

lines.speaker: sandra
lines.text: Did you put the seat down?
lines.how: brisk, sideways, as if it is any other morning

lines.speaker: derek
lines.how: after a long beat; defeated, fond

beats.name: Over the brow
beats.blurb: From behind the hundred at the crest: the AI's building in the fold of the downs below. They stop.

lines.speaker: ai
lines.voice: Suno Voice "badcode newsreader" (the AI), dry, through Maddie's speaker: small-speaker filter, beacon pulses on his words
lines.text: I tried to make it nice.
lines.how: a little shy, hopeful, the first time he has hosted anyone

beats.name: Mind the step
beats.blurb: At the building: the amber seam has opened into a doorway with one low step. Maddie stops at it. The AI asks them in.

lines.speaker: ai
lines.voice: Suno Voice "badcode newsreader" (the AI), dry, through Maddie's speaker: small-speaker filter, beacon pulses on his words
lines.how: warm, precise, a host at his own door

frames.purpose: The turn of the scene in one act: the woman who kept the machine on the step (scene B) comes out to the step herself, straightens its torn bunting, and sends it first. Trust given by a hand, not argued. The step itself is saved for C07.

still.prompt: Using the first image for the old woman, the second image for the place and the third for the robot: a low medium shot from just outside the bunker, at the height of a small robot, of the old woman from the first image, the same face, grey hair in a bun, glasses and green cable-knit cardigan, who has just stepped out of the dark doorway between the open green steel blast doors into grey daylight and stopped on the concrete step beside the small grey six-wheeled delivery robot from the third image, its amber beacon lit and the torn, faded cloth bunting hanging across its front wheels. She is bending slightly, one hand reaching down to straighten the robot's torn bunting, her eyes on the open downs beyond the lens, mouth closed. Behind her, in the shadow of the tunnel, the faces of other survivors in worn jumpers and coats wait to come out. motion.prompt: The camera does not move. The old woman straightens the robot's torn bunting with one hand, gives it a small pat, then straightens up, looks out at the downs and speaks, dry and calm. She says: Go on, then. You lead. Then she closes her mouth and holds still. The robot's amber beacon pulses once. The people behind her in the dark stay still. The camera does not move.

In the near foreground an old man with a walking stick is being helped to sit down on the wet grass by a younger man with a hand on his shoulder, exhausted, and beside them a shopping trolley piled with blankets lies tipped over in the mud. Below them the land falls away into a fold of the downs, and in it lies a long, low building of black glass, many times longer than it is tall, with one single thin horizontal seam of warm amber light running its whole length, set down in a fold between two green chalk downs, the only made thing in sight; no windows, no signs, no other lights. Cloud shadows lie across the downs. On the crest at the front of the crowd, small, the small grey six-wheeled delivery robot from the third image, its amber beacon lit and the torn, faded cloth bunting hanging across its front wheels.
